# 26. AI AND INTELLIGENT ACCOUNTING ASSISTANCE

## 26.1 Permitted assistance

AI or machine-learning components may assist with:

- Suggested account classification.
- Description normalization.
- Anomaly detection.
- Duplicate-pattern detection.
- Source-document extraction.
- Unusual adjustment detection.
- Suggested reconciliation candidates.
- Explanation generation.
- Forecasting.
- Exception prioritization.
- Natural-language reporting.

## 26.2 Authority restrictions

AI must not independently:

- Create or approve accounting policies.
- Change a chart of accounts.
- Grant posting privileges.
- Bypass approval requirements.
- Alter posted journal entries.
- Reopen closed periods.
- Suppress integrity violations.
- Declare a reconciliation case resolved.
- Fabricate missing financial evidence.
- Commit unauthorized accounting adjustments.

## 26.3 Human and policy control

AI-generated suggestions must be distinguishable from authoritative accounting facts.

Where automated classification is permitted, the governing policy must specify:

- Eligible transaction classes.
- Required evidence.
- Confidence or validation criteria where relevant.
- Approval conditions.
- Monitoring.
- Audit requirements.
- Fallback behavior.
- Model version.
- Evaluation and rollback procedures.

A confidence score alone is not proof of accounting correctness.

## 26.4 Model governance

Any model affecting accounting classification or controls must have:

- Identifiable ownership.
- Versioned deployment.
- Evaluation evidence.
- Drift monitoring.
- Change approval.
- Reproducibility requirements appropriate to the use case.
- Incident handling.
- Rollback capability.
- Explicit authority boundaries.

---

# 27. EXTENSIBILITY AND PLUGIN ARCHITECTURE

## 27.1 Extension principles

The accounting capability must support extensions without modifying unrelated canonical domains or weakening ledger invariants.

Potential extension categories include:

- Source adapters.
- Accounting rule providers.
- External account mappings.
- Currency valuation providers.
- Reporting adapters.
- Evidence providers.
- Regulatory export adapters.
- Specialized accounting dimensions.
- Industry-specific posting policies.

## 27.2 Extension contract

Every extension must declare:

- Canonical extension identifier.
- Owner.
- Version.
- Capability.
- Input schema.
- Output schema.
- Dependencies.
- Required permissions.
- Data classification.
- Failure behavior.
- Compatibility requirements.
- Validation tests.
- Security requirements.
- Lifecycle state.
- Retirement policy.

## 27.3 Extension restrictions

An extension must not:

- Modify posted records directly.
- Bypass the posting authorization gate.
- Introduce an alternative canonical account identity.
- Change balancing semantics without authorization.
- Override an approved accounting policy without governance.
- Create circular dependencies.
- Store an independent competing source of accounting truth.

## 27.4 Discovery

The architecture should support automatic discovery of compatible extensions through approved registries.

Discovery must validate declared capabilities, dependencies, version compatibility, and authorization before activation.

---

# 28. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

The following requirements are proposed and require canonical reconciliation.

## 28.1 Ledger foundation

**MPS-021-FR-001 — Ledger Identity**

The system shall provide a unique canonical identity for every approved ledger.

**MPS-021-FR-002 — Accounting Entity Binding**

Every ledger shall be associated with a valid accounting entity or explicitly governed equivalent.

**MPS-021-FR-003 — Ledger Policy Binding**

Every ledger shall resolve its applicable accounting, posting, currency, and period policies.

**MPS-021-FR-004 — Chart of Accounts**

The system shall support governed account definitions and effective-dated account changes.

**MPS-021-FR-005 — Journal Definitions**

The system shall support configurable journal classifications and posting constraints.

## 28.2 Source intake

**MPS-021-FR-006 — Authorized Intake**

The system shall accept source facts only through authenticated and authorized interfaces.

**MPS-021-FR-007 — Source Validation**

The system shall validate source identity, required fields, schema version, and applicable accounting context.

**MPS-021-FR-008 — Idempotent Intake**

The system shall prevent duplicate processing of the same logical source event.

**MPS-021-FR-009 — Invalid Source Handling**

The system shall reject or quarantine invalid source facts with traceable reasons.

**MPS-021-FR-010 — Source Lineage**

The system shall retain references connecting accounting records to their originating source facts.

## 28.3 Accounting classification

**MPS-021-FR-011 — Governed Rule Selection**

The system shall select an approved posting rule applicable to the source fact and effective date.

**MPS-021-FR-012 — Rule Version Preservation**

The system shall retain the posting-rule version used to construct a journal entry.

**MPS-021-FR-013 — Missing Rule Handling**

The system shall not post a source fact when a required accounting rule is unavailable.

**MPS-021-FR-014 — Explainable Classification**

The system shall provide an auditable explanation of the rule and mapping used for a posting.

**MPS-021-FR-015 — Deterministic Evaluation**

Equivalent inputs evaluated under the same deterministic rule version shall produce equivalent classification outcomes.

## 28.4 Journal construction and posting

**MPS-021-FR-016 — Journal Construction**

The system shall construct journal entries from validated source facts and approved posting rules.

**MPS-021-FR-017 — Balanced Posting**

The system shall enforce the applicable ledger balancing invariant before posting.

**MPS-021-FR-018 — Atomic Commit**

The system shall commit the required journal entry and lines atomically according to the approved persistence model.

**MPS-021-FR-019 — Posting Authorization**

The system shall enforce applicable authorization and approval requirements before commit.

**MPS-021-FR-020 — Durable Posting Status**

The system shall distinguish a durable posting from an accepted, pending, or failed request.

## 28.5 Currency and accounting periods

**MPS-021-FR-021 — Explicit Currency Context**

The system shall retain transaction currency and other required currency contexts explicitly.

**MPS-021-FR-022 — Governed Rounding**

The system shall apply the approved precision and rounding rules for each applicable accounting context.

**MPS-021-FR-023 — Period Validation**

The system shall validate the target accounting period before committing a posting.

**MPS-021-FR-024 — Closed-Period Protection**

The system shall prevent unauthorized posting to a closed accounting period.

**MPS-021-FR-025 — Controlled Reopening**

The system shall enforce authorization and audit requirements for period reopening.

## 28.6 Corrections and projections

**MPS-021-FR-026 — Immutable Posted Records**

The system shall prohibit unauthorized mutation or deletion of posted accounting entries.

**MPS-021-FR-027 — Governed Reversal**

The system shall support authorized reversal entries linked to original postings.

**MPS-021-FR-028 — Governed Adjustment**

The system shall support approved accounting adjustments with reason and evidence.

**MPS-021-FR-029 — Rebuildable Projections**

The system shall support rebuilding derived balances from authoritative accounting records.

**MPS-021-FR-030 — Projection Integrity**

The system shall detect and report material inconsistencies between authoritative postings and derived projections.

## 28.7 Integration and reconciliation

**MPS-021-FR-031 — External Mapping**

The system shall support versioned mappings to approved external accounting systems.

**MPS-021-FR-032 — Duplicate Export Prevention**

The system shall prevent repeated export requests from creating uncontrolled duplicate accounting consequences.

**MPS-021-FR-033 — Export Status**

The system shall track external export states and distinguish acknowledgment from verified external posting.

**MPS-021-FR-034 — Reconciliation Integration**

The system shall expose authorized accounting records and references to the canonical reconciliation capability.

**MPS-021-FR-035 — Correction Traceability**

The system shall preserve relationships between original entries, corrections, reversals, and relevant reconciliation references.

## 28.8 Security and audit

**MPS-021-FR-036 — Least Privilege**

The system shall enforce least-privilege access for accounting operations.

**MPS-021-FR-037 — Separation of Duties**

The system shall enforce applicable segregation-of-duties requirements.

**MPS-021-FR-038 — Auditability**

The system shall preserve required evidence for postings, corrections, approvals, configuration changes, and period operations.

**MPS-021-FR-039 — Sensitive-Data Protection**

The system shall minimize and protect sensitive information in accounting records and integration payloads.

**MPS-021-FR-040 — Integrity Monitoring**

The system shall detect and surface defined accounting integrity violations.

## 28.9 Operations and extensibility

**MPS-021-FR-041 — Failure Recovery**

The system shall support governed retry, quarantine, recovery, and escalation for failed operations.

**MPS-021-FR-042 — Event Integrity**

The system shall publish accounting lifecycle events consistently with authoritative commit state.

**MPS-021-FR-043 — Operational Observability**

The system shall expose operational and integrity metrics for authorized monitoring.

**MPS-021-FR-044 — Extension Contracts**

The system shall validate extension metadata, dependencies, permissions, and compatibility.

**MPS-021-FR-045 — Historical Reproducibility**

The system shall retain sufficient information to explain historical postings under the applicable historical rules.

## 28.10 Governance and reporting

**MPS-021-FR-046 — Period Close Evidence**

The system shall preserve the evidence required for approved accounting-period closure.

**MPS-021-FR-047 — Governed Statements**

The system shall generate accounting statements from authoritative records and approved reporting definitions.

**MPS-021-FR-048 — Versioned Schemas**

The system shall support governed schema evolution without silently changing the meaning of historical records.

**MPS-021-FR-049 — Context Assimilation**

The system shall require canonical context reconciliation before implementation authorization.

**MPS-021-FR-050 — Evidence-Based Certification**

The system shall not be certified until required functional, security, accounting-integrity, recovery, and governance evidence has been reviewed and approved.

---

# 29. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

The following acceptance criteria are proposed. They have not been executed or passed.

**MPS-021-AC-001**

Every approved ledger resolves to one valid canonical identity.

**MPS-021-AC-002**

A ledger without a valid accounting context cannot accept a posting.

**MPS-021-AC-003**

Unauthorized changes to account definitions are rejected and audited.

**MPS-021-AC-004**

A journal referencing an invalid account is rejected before posting.

**MPS-021-AC-005**

An invalid source schema is rejected or quarantined with an explicit reason.

**MPS-021-AC-006**

Repeated delivery of the same source event does not create duplicate journal entries.

**MPS-021-AC-007**

A source fact without a required approved posting rule cannot be posted.

**MPS-021-AC-008**

A posted entry retains the exact posting-rule version used during construction.

**MPS-021-AC-009**

Equivalent source facts evaluated under the same deterministic rule version produce equivalent accounting classifications.

**MPS-021-AC-010**

A journal that violates its applicable balancing invariant cannot be posted.

**MPS-021-AC-011**

A journal cannot be partially committed with missing required lines.

**MPS-021-AC-012**

A caller lacking posting authority cannot commit a journal entry.

**MPS-021-AC-013**

A timeout after a successful commit does not cause a duplicate posting when the caller retries.

**MPS-021-AC-014**

The API distinguishes accepted, pending, rejected, and durably posted states.

**MPS-021-AC-015**

Currency conversion retains the original amount and currency.

**MPS-021-AC-016**

Currency rounding follows the applicable approved precision and rounding policy.

**MPS-021-AC-017**

A posting targeting a closed period is rejected or routed through the approved exception workflow.

**MPS-021-AC-018**

A period cannot be reopened without the required authorization and audit evidence.

**MPS-021-AC-019**

A posted journal entry cannot be silently edited or deleted.

**MPS-021-AC-020**

A reversal references its original journal entry and preserves both records.

**MPS-021-AC-021**

A correction without required evidence or approval cannot be committed.

**MPS-021-AC-022**

A projection rebuild produces balances consistent with the authoritative journal records under the same accounting rules.

**MPS-021-AC-023**

A projection rebuild does not create new accounting postings.

**MPS-021-AC-024**

An external mapping change preserves its prior version and effective-date history.

**MPS-021-AC-025**

Repeated export delivery does not create uncontrolled duplicate external postings.

**MPS-021-AC-026**

An external acknowledgment is not represented as verified posting unless the integration contract supports that conclusion.

**MPS-021-AC-027**

Reconciliation findings can be linked to accounting records without directly mutating posted entries.

**MPS-021-AC-028**

An authorized accounting correction preserves links to the original entry and related discrepancy.

**MPS-021-AC-029**

Users without appropriate access cannot read restricted accounting records.

**MPS-021-AC-030**

Sensitive information is excluded from payloads where it is not necessary for the accounting purpose.

**MPS-021-AC-031**

A user cannot approve a transaction when the applicable separation-of-duties policy prohibits the approval.

**MPS-021-AC-032**

Posting-rule changes are versioned and auditable.

**MPS-021-AC-033**

A critical accounting integrity violation generates an observable incident or alert according to the approved policy.

**MPS-021-AC-034**

Failed accounting source facts remain discoverable and have a documented disposition.

**MPS-021-AC-035**

Projection lag is observable through operational metrics.

**MPS-021-AC-036**

The event publication mechanism does not publish a committed-posting event before the corresponding posting is durable.

**MPS-021-AC-037**

Replaying projection events does not create duplicate journal entries.

**MPS-021-AC-038**

Historical postings remain explainable after a posting-rule update.

**MPS-021-AC-039**

Period closure produces retained evidence of the applied checks and required approvals.

**MPS-021-AC-040**

Accounting statements identify their scope, period, currency, and data-finality context.

**MPS-021-AC-041**

Concurrent posting requests preserve the required uniqueness and balancing invariants.

**MPS-021-AC-042**

A failure during journal persistence leaves no externally visible partial committed entry.

**MPS-021-AC-043**

A recovery operation does not bypass authorization, idempotency, or period restrictions.

**MPS-021-AC-044**

An extension lacking required permissions or compatibility declarations cannot be activated.

**MPS-021-AC-045**

The system rejects unauthorized attempts to bypass the accounting posting gate.

**MPS-021-AC-046**

The system can trace a posted entry to its originating source fact and applicable accounting policy.

**MPS-021-AC-047**

A material discrepancy between a projection and authoritative journal records can be detected and investigated.

**MPS-021-AC-048**

Schema evolution preserves the defined interpretation of historical records.

**MPS-021-AC-049**

Implementation authorization remains blocked until the Context Assimilation Gate is approved.

**MPS-021-AC-050**

Certification is withheld until the required test results, audit evidence, and authorized approvals exist.

# 30. PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS

The following ADRs are required decision topics. Their outcomes are not yet approved.

**MPS-021-ADR-001 — Canonical Accounting Ownership**

Determine whether this capability is the authoritative ledger, a specialized subledger, or a governed integration boundary over existing accounting infrastructure.

**MPS-021-ADR-002 — Ledger Topology**

Determine the canonical model for entities, ledgers, books, and organizational boundaries.

**MPS-021-ADR-003 — Double-Entry Enforcement**

Determine the balancing unit, permitted exceptions, and technical enforcement model.

**MPS-021-ADR-004 — Chart of Accounts Authority**

Determine whether account definitions are owned locally or by an existing canonical accounting registry.

**MPS-021-ADR-005 — Posting Rule Governance**

Determine rule ownership, versioning, approval, deployment, and historical execution semantics.

**MPS-021-ADR-006 — Posting Commit Boundary**

Determine the atomic commit model for headers, lines, idempotency, and required metadata.

**MPS-021-ADR-007 — Source Event Semantics**

Determine the required source event contracts and source-fact immutability model.

**MPS-021-ADR-008 — Idempotency Model**

Determine key construction, retention, conflict handling, and uniqueness scope.

**MPS-021-ADR-009 — Currency Representation**

Determine canonical monetary types, precision, conversion references, and valuation policy integration.

**MPS-021-ADR-010 — Accounting Period Model**

Determine period calendars, close controls, reopening, and backdated adjustment semantics.

**MPS-021-ADR-011 — Correction Model**

Determine reversal, compensating entry, reclassification, and adjustment workflows.

**MPS-021-ADR-012 — Projection Architecture**

Determine balance projections, rebuild semantics, integrity checks, and acceptable lag.

**MPS-021-ADR-013 — External Accounting Integration**

Determine the canonical export/import model, mapping authority, and external idempotency strategy.

**MPS-021-ADR-014 — Reconciliation Boundary**

Determine the precise contract between the ledger and the canonical reconciliation capability.

**MPS-021-ADR-015 — Event Publication**

Determine the durable commit-to-event publication mechanism.

**MPS-021-ADR-016 — Audit Evidence**

Determine the canonical audit service, evidence retention, integrity controls, and access model.

**MPS-021-ADR-017 — Data Retention**

Determine retention, archival, deletion restrictions, legal holds, and privacy controls.

**MPS-021-ADR-018 — Query and Reporting Isolation**

Determine how accounting reads and reporting workloads are isolated from authoritative posting workloads.

**MPS-021-ADR-019 — Recovery Objectives**

Determine measurable recovery-point and recovery-time objectives.

**MPS-021-ADR-020 — Security and Separation of Duties**

Determine the approved role model and mandatory approval separation.

**MPS-021-ADR-021 — Extension Discovery**

Determine registry ownership, extension validation, compatibility, and activation semantics.

**MPS-021-ADR-022 — AI-Assisted Classification**

Determine whether AI classification is permitted, under which controls, and for which transaction classes.

**MPS-021-ADR-023 — Ledger Partitioning**

Determine partitioning boundaries without weakening uniqueness, traceability, or balancing guarantees.

**MPS-021-ADR-024 — External System of Record**

Determine how this ledger interacts with any existing enterprise accounting system and whether the authoritative boundary is a subledger or general ledger.

**MPS-021-ADR-025 — Certification Model**

Determine the evidence required for architectural approval, accounting-integrity verification, operational readiness, and production authorization.

# 32. TRACEABILITY AND LINEAGE

## 32.1 Required lineage chain

The architecture must support the following logical traceability chain:

SOURCE BUSINESS FACT
        |
        v
SOURCE EVENT OR AUTHORIZED COMMAND
        |
        v
SOURCE FACT REFERENCE
        |
        v
ACCOUNTING POLICY AND RULE VERSION
        |
        v
CLASSIFICATION DECISION
        |
        v
JOURNAL ENTRY
        |
        v
JOURNAL LINES
        |
        v
ACCOUNT BALANCE PROJECTION
        |
        v
ACCOUNTING STATEMENT OR REPORT

Additional lineage may connect:

- Original posting to reversal.
- Original posting to adjustment.
- Posting to external export.
- Posting to reconciliation reference.
- Posting to accounting period close.
- Posting to audit evidence.
- Posting to external accounting acknowledgment.

## 32.2 Lineage requirements

The system must support answering:

- Which source facts caused this posting?
- Which accounting policy was applied?
- Which posting rule version was used?
- Who or what authorized the posting?
- Which accounts were affected?
- Which period was used?
- Which currency conversion was applied?
- Was the entry corrected or reversed?
- Was the entry included in an external export?
- Which reconciliation records reference it?
- Which statements or reports include it?
- What evidence supports its accounting treatment?

## 32.3 Knowledge Once Principle

Canonical accounting definitions must be authored once in their authoritative locations.

Consumers must reference canonical account, currency, entity, policy, and ledger identities rather than independently defining competing versions.

Local caches and projections may exist when necessary, but they must have explicit ownership, refresh, and consistency rules.

# 33. TESTING AND VERIFICATION STRATEGY

## 33.1 Test categories

The implementation must include:

- Unit tests.
- Schema-validation tests.
- Posting-rule tests.
- Accounting invariant tests.
- Journal balancing tests.
- Idempotency tests.
- Authorization tests.
- Separation-of-duties tests.
- Period-state tests.
- Currency and rounding tests.
- Correction and reversal tests.
- Integration tests.
- Event-delivery tests.
- Projection rebuild tests.
- Concurrency tests.
- Failure-injection tests.
- Disaster-recovery tests.
- Security tests.
- Performance tests.
- Historical reproducibility tests.
- Audit-evidence tests.
- Regression tests.
- Migration tests where applicable.

## 33.2 Essential negative tests

The system must demonstrate safe rejection or controlled handling of:

1. An unbalanced journal.
2. An unauthorized posting.
3. A duplicate source event.
4. An invalid account reference.
5. A missing posting rule.
6. A closed-period posting attempt.
7. A stale or unauthorized rule version.
8. A correction without required approval.
9. An external export retry after an ambiguous response.
10. A projection rebuild during active posting.
11. An unauthorized period reopening.
12. An invalid currency conversion reference.
13. An extension with undeclared dependencies.
14. A replay of previously committed accounting events.
15. A failed audit-evidence persistence operation.

## 33.3 Reproducibility tests

For a historical posting, the system must be able to reconstruct the relevant:

- Source facts.
- Accounting context.
- Policy version.
- Posting-rule version.
- Classification result.
- Journal entry.
- Journal lines.
- Authorization evidence.
- Correction lineage.

The exact reconstruction model must respect privacy, retention, and legal obligations.

## 33.4 Verification integrity

Test evidence must identify:

- Test suite version.
- Code version.
- Configuration version.
- Accounting policy version.
- Test environment.
- Test data.
- Execution time.
- Results.
- Failures.
- Exceptions.
- Reviewer.
- Approval status.

A test result from one code or configuration version must not be presented as evidence for an untested version.

# 34. IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACTS AND BOUNDARIES

## 34.1 Contract-first implementation

Before implementation, the architecture must define and approve:

- Canonical entity definitions.
- Account and journal schemas.
- Source event contracts.
- Posting command contracts.
- Posting result semantics.
- Accounting policy interfaces.
- Rule evaluation contracts.
- Authorization contracts.
- Period management contracts.
- Correction contracts.
- External integration contracts.
- Reconciliation contracts.
- Event schemas.
- Error taxonomy.
- Idempotency semantics.
- Recovery semantics.
- Audit requirements.
- Versioning rules.

## 34.2 Required invariants

Every implementation must preserve these invariants:

1. One designated authority for each canonical accounting record.
2. No unauthorized posting.
3. No uncontrolled duplicate posting.
4. No partial committed journal.
5. No silent mutation of posted history.
6. No undocumented currency conversion.
7. No unauthorized closed-period posting.
8. No missing correction lineage.
9. No untracked projection divergence.
10. No uncontrolled external replay.
11. No bypass of canonical authorization.
12. No implementation before Context Assimilation Gate approval.
13. No certification without evidence.
14. No technology-specific assumptions in canonical domain contracts unless approved as implementation decisions.

## 34.3 Technology-selection neutrality

The architecture must not mandate a particular:

- Programming language.
- Framework.
- Database.
- Message broker.
- Cloud provider.
- Infrastructure platform.
- Accounting vendor.
- Payment processor.
- API protocol.
- Identity provider.
- Analytics engine.

Technology choices must be documented as implementation decisions after the canonical contracts and operational constraints are known.

## 34.4 Implementation sequence

Proposed implementation sequence:

PHASE 0 — Canonical Context Assimilation
PHASE 1 — Ownership and Domain Contracts
PHASE 2 — Ledger and Account Model
PHASE 3 — Source Intake and Idempotency
PHASE 4 — Posting Rules and Journal Construction
PHASE 5 — Authorization and Atomic Commit
PHASE 6 — Balances and Projections
PHASE 7 — Corrections and Period Management
PHASE 8 — Reconciliation and External Integrations
PHASE 9 — Reporting, Observability, and Recovery
PHASE 10 — Security, Performance, and Certification

The sequence may be refined after dependency analysis.

No implementation phase is authorized merely by appearing in this document.

---

# 35. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

## 35.1 Integrity

Financial integrity takes precedence over convenience, ungoverned throughput, and silent degradation.

## 35.2 Availability

The architecture must support business-approved availability objectives without compromising required accounting invariants.

## 35.3 Performance

The system must meet approved posting, query, recovery, and reporting SLOs established through measured workloads.

## 35.4 Scalability

Growth must not require redesigning the canonical accounting ontology for each new merchant, currency, industry, or integration.

## 35.5 Security

Financial data and posting capabilities must be protected by canonical identity, authorization, encryption, audit, and monitoring controls.

## 35.6 Auditability

Financial activity must be traceable from source facts to posted accounting effects and downstream representations.

## 35.7 Maintainability

Accounting rules, mappings, schemas, and integrations must be versioned and governed rather than scattered across unrelated code paths.

## 35.8 Interoperability

External integrations must use explicit, versioned contracts and canonical identifiers.

## 35.9 Portability

The logical architecture must remain independent of a specific vendor, cloud, database, or runtime.

## 35.10 Recoverability

The system must provide tested recovery procedures for data, posting workflows, projections, and integrations.

## 35.11 Observability

Critical accounting operations must expose traceable outcomes, metrics, and actionable failure information.

## 35.12 Explainability

The system must be able to explain how a posted accounting record was constructed from approved source facts and rules.

## 35.13 Compatibility

Schema and policy evolution must preserve the defined interpretation of historical accounting records.

## 35.14 Privacy

Accounting traceability must not become a justification for retaining unnecessary personal or sensitive data.

## 35.15 Governance

Every material accounting capability must have an identified owner, approval model, lifecycle, and evidence requirements.

---

# 37. ABSOLUTE ARCHITECTURAL PROHIBITIONS

The following behaviors are prohibited unless a formally approved canonical exception explicitly governs them.

1. Creating a second competing canonical accounting ledger without an approved ownership model.
2. Silently editing or deleting posted accounting entries.
3. Posting unbalanced journal entries where the approved model requires balance.
4. Posting without required authorization.
5. Allowing duplicate source delivery to create duplicate financial consequences.
6. Treating payment authorization as proof of completed cash movement.
7. Treating a settlement obligation as proof of completed payout.
8. Treating a reconciliation result as permission to rewrite accounting records.
9. Using floating-point approximations for authoritative monetary calculations without a proven safe representation.
10. Silently changing historical currency conversion values.
11. Silently moving postings out of closed accounting periods.
12. Deleting account definitions required to interpret historical records.
13. Allowing AI to bypass accounting controls.
14. Granting extensions unrestricted posting authority.
15. Allowing reporting workloads to compromise posting integrity.
16. Publishing a posted event before its authoritative posting is durable.
17. Replaying accounting events without explicit duplicate-prevention semantics.
18. Exposing sensitive source information unnecessarily.
19. Hard-coding one accounting standard or jurisdiction into the universal domain model.
20. Hard-coding one accounting vendor or database into canonical contracts.
21. Introducing duplicate account, currency, entity, or policy registries without approved authority.
22. Hiding failed or quarantined accounting source facts.
23. Certifying untested accounting behavior.
24. Claiming implementation without verified implementation evidence.
25. Beginning implementation before canonical context reconciliation.
26. Creating a new canonical concept without checking whether it already exists.
27. Introducing circular dependencies between accounting, settlement, payment, and reconciliation.
28. Allowing external-system acknowledgments to imply stronger guarantees than their contracts provide.
29. Treating derived account balances as a substitute for authoritative journal history.
30. Allowing operational convenience to override mandatory accounting, security, or governance controls.

---

# 38. ARCHITECTURAL COMPLETENESS MODEL

This specification defines a proposed accounting architecture, but the completeness of the implementation cannot be established from document content alone.

The following dimensions must be evaluated independently.

| Dimension | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Constitutional completeness | Approved alignment with UCOS constitutions and laws |
| Domain completeness | Reconciled accounting responsibilities and boundaries |
| Ontology completeness | Approved canonical accounting concepts and relationships |
| Identifier completeness | Registered and collision-free identifiers |
| Accounting integrity | Verified posting, balancing, correction, and immutability controls |
| Functional completeness | Requirements mapped to implemented capabilities and tests |
| API completeness | Approved contracts and compatibility evidence |
| Event completeness | Registered event schemas and delivery semantics |
| Security completeness | Threat model and verified security controls |
| Financial control completeness | Approved authorization, period-close, and adjustment controls |
| Currency completeness | Verified monetary representation and valuation behavior |
| Integration completeness | Tested source and external accounting contracts |
| Recovery completeness | Demonstrated backup, restoration, and recovery behavior |
| Operational completeness | Monitoring, runbooks, ownership, and incident procedures |
| Historical completeness | Demonstrated lineage and reproducibility |
| Reporting completeness | Validated statements and accounting outputs |
| Governance completeness | Approved ownership, policies, lifecycle, and change control |
| Technology neutrality | Canonical contracts independent of unapproved vendor choices |
| Certification completeness | Retained evidence for all mandatory gates |

No percentage of completeness should be claimed without an agreed measurement model, evidence, and authorized assessment.

# 41. PROPOSED FINAL ACCOUNTING FLOW

The intended logical flow is:

1. An authoritative business domain establishes a valid source fact.
2. The source fact is transmitted through a governed interface.
3. The accounting intake validates identity, schema, authorization, and context.
4. Idempotency controls determine whether the fact has already been processed.
5. The classification engine resolves the applicable approved accounting rule.
6. The posting engine constructs a journal entry.
7. Currency, period, account, and balancing invariants are validated.
8. The authorization gate enforces required approval.
9. The ledger commits the journal entry and required lines atomically.
10. The system records the posting outcome and provenance.
11. Accounting events are published consistently with the durable commit.
12. Balance projections are updated.
13. Accounting records become available to authorized reports and reconciliation processes.
14. External exports are generated where required.
15. Export results are tracked independently of the authoritative posting.
16. Reconciliation evaluates independent financial records.
17. Discrepancies initiate governed investigation and correction workflows.
18. Corrections create new linked accounting facts.
19. Period-close controls verify required accounting conditions.
20. Approved statements and reports are generated from the governed accounting model.
21. Audit evidence and lineage remain available according to approved policies.

At every step, the system must distinguish authoritative facts from proposals, derived projections, external acknowledgments, and reconciliation conclusions.

The objective is to establish one coherent, governed accounting capability that records authorized financial consequences, preserves immutable historical evidence, enforces accounting integrity, and interoperates with payment, settlement, reconciliation, merchant, tax, reporting, and external accounting capabilities without duplicating their authority.

- One authoritative accounting record for each governed accounting fact.

- No untraceable accounting adjustments.

- No technology, vendor, cloud, or database lock-in in the canonical domain model.

# 1. EXECUTIVE PURPOSE

## 1.1 Purpose

Establish a universal, governed, extensible financial reporting and decision-intelligence capability for the UCOS Universal Marketplace.

The capability must transform authorized financial and commercial facts into trustworthy, explainable, reproducible, appropriately scoped, and decision-useful financial information.

It must enable authorized stakeholders to understand:

- What financial activity occurred.
- What accounting consequences were recorded.
- What revenue was recognized under applicable policies.
- What amounts are owed to merchants.
- What settlement obligations exist.
- What payments and payouts were executed.
- What refunds and reversals occurred.
- What commissions and fees were earned.
- What taxes were determined or recorded.
- What financial exceptions remain unresolved.
- What amounts remain unreconciled.
- What commercial arrangements affect financial performance.
- What financial trends are emerging.
- What financial risks require attention.
- What forecasts can reasonably be produced from available evidence.
- What decisions are supported by the available data.
- What limitations or uncertainties affect a financial conclusion.

The system must provide these capabilities without becoming a competing accounting ledger, payment system, settlement engine, reconciliation authority, tax engine, or commercial decision authority.

## 1.2 Fundamental objective

Every financial report, statement, metric, dashboard, forecast, and analytical conclusion must have a clearly defined meaning, source, scope, calculation method, authorization model, and freshness status.

A report must not present an unverified estimate as an authoritative financial fact.

A dashboard must not silently combine amounts that have incompatible:

- Accounting bases.
- Currencies.
- Periods.
- Recognition rules.
- Transaction states.
- Entity boundaries.
- Data-finality states.
- Tax treatments.
- Merchant ownership contexts.
- Reconciliation statuses.

Where complete data is unavailable, the system must disclose the limitation rather than silently inventing or extrapolating missing values.

## 1.3 Architectural objective

The target is a reporting capability that can serve multiple marketplace business models, legal entities, industries, currencies, organizational structures, and operational environments through reusable canonical reporting abstractions.

The architecture must support both standardized reporting and governed customization.

It must remain:

- Domain-agnostic where appropriate.
- Technology-agnostic.
- Database-agnostic.
- Cloud-agnostic.
- Vendor-neutral.
- Protocol-extensible.
- Policy-driven.
- Discoverable.
- Auditable.
- Scalable.
- Secure.
- Historically reproducible.

Universality must come from canonical concepts, metadata, policies, contracts, and reusable analytical capabilities—not from hard-coded lists of merchants, industries, countries, currencies, report types, or business models.

---

# 2. CONSTITUTIONAL FOUNDATION

## 2.1 Constitutional authority

This capability operates under the applicable UCOS constitutional hierarchy.

It must comply with the approved authority boundaries of:

- Universal identity.
- Access governance.
- Financial accounting.
- Commercial transactions.
- Payment execution.
- Tax determination.
- Settlement.
- Reconciliation.
- Data governance.
- Audit.
- Security.
- Regulatory compliance.
- Information management.
- Reporting governance.

The final hierarchy and ownership boundaries must be reconciled with the authoritative UCOS architecture.

## 2.2 Proposed constitutional laws

The following laws are proposed for registration and reconciliation.

### UMFRA-001 — Reporting Is Not Accounting Authority

A financial report is a representation of authoritative source facts or derived calculations.

A report must not create, modify, or replace authoritative accounting records.

### UMFRA-002 — One Canonical Meaning per Metric

Every canonical financial metric must have one approved semantic definition within its governed scope.

Multiple presentations may exist, but they must not silently redefine the metric.

### UMFRA-003 — Provenance Preservation

Every material financial result must be traceable to its source records, transformations, calculation definitions, and applicable policies.

### UMFRA-004 — Explicit Scope

Every report must define or resolve its applicable entity, period, currency, accounting basis, transaction scope, and data-finality context.

### UMFRA-005 — No Silent Mixing

Financial amounts with incompatible semantic or accounting contexts must not be combined without an approved transformation or explicit disclosure.

### UMFRA-006 — Reproducible Calculations

A governed report must be reproducible under its recorded source snapshot or version, metric definitions, calculation rules, and reporting parameters, subject to documented limitations.

### UMFRA-007 — Authorized Disclosure

Financial information must be accessible only to authorized principals within the applicable data, entity, merchant, organizational, and reporting scope.

### UMFRA-008 — Source Authority Preservation

The reporting capability must consume authoritative records from their designated owners rather than create competing canonical records.

### UMFRA-009 — Explicit Data Freshness

Every report must disclose its relevant freshness or finality state when the state materially affects interpretation.

### UMFRA-010 — No False Finality

Pending, estimated, provisional, incomplete, or unreconciled financial information must not be represented as final without an approved basis.

### UMFRA-011 — Governed Metric Evolution

Changes to canonical metric definitions must be versioned, reviewed, approved, and traceable.

### UMFRA-012 — Controlled Historical Restatement

Historical reports must not be silently rewritten when source records, policies, or calculation definitions change.

Any permitted restatement must be explicitly identified and traceable.

### UMFRA-013 — Separation of Fact and Forecast

Observed financial facts, accounting projections, forecasts, simulations, and AI-generated estimates must be distinguishable.

### UMFRA-014 — No Unauthorized Inference

The system must not infer sensitive personal attributes or generate unauthorized financial conclusions merely because underlying data is technically accessible.

### UMFRA-015 — Explainable Aggregation

Every material aggregation must identify the applicable inclusion, exclusion, grouping, conversion, and calculation rules.

### UMFRA-016 — Privacy-Preserving Analytics

Analytical usefulness must not justify unnecessary disclosure or retention of personal or sensitive information.

### UMFRA-017 — Governed Report Publication

Publication, distribution, export, and external sharing of financial reports must follow approved authorization and disclosure policies.

### UMFRA-018 — Deterministic Financial Arithmetic

Authoritative monetary calculations must use an approved precision, rounding, and currency model.

### UMFRA-019 — Reconciliation Independence

Reporting may display reconciliation outcomes but must not determine or modify reconciliation conclusions outside the reconciliation authority.

### UMFRA-020 — Context Before Implementation

Implementation must not begin until relevant canonical context, metric definitions, ownership boundaries, identifiers, dependencies, and existing reporting capabilities have been reconciled.

### UMFRA-021 — Evidence-Based Certification

No report, dashboard, metric, forecast, or reporting capability may be declared certified without appropriate validation evidence and authorized approval.

## 3.3 Critical distinctions

- Gross merchandise value.

- Purchase commitment value.
- Payment authorization amount.
- Payment capture amount.
- Cash received.
- Accounting revenue.

- Settlement obligation.
- Settlement amount executed.
- Payout amount.
- Refund amount.
- Tax amount.
- Marketplace commission.
- Recognized expense.
- Accounting balance.
- Available balance.
- Reconciled amount.
- Forecast revenue.
- Estimated future cash flow.

These measures may be related, but they are not interchangeable.

A metric catalog must define their meanings and prevent ambiguous labels from concealing semantic differences.

# 4. CANONICAL REPORTING ONTOLOGY

## 4.1 Reporting Artifact

A Reporting Artifact is a governed representation used to communicate, inspect, analyze, or distribute data.

Examples include:

- Financial statement.
- Merchant statement.
- Financial dashboard.
- Operational financial report.
- Regulatory report.
- Accounting report.
- Analytical report.
- Forecast.
- Scenario analysis.
- Financial exception report.

Each artifact must have a canonical identity, owner, lifecycle, access policy, and versioning model.

## 4.2 Report Definition

A Report Definition describes how a report is constructed.

It may include:

- Report identifier.
- Name.
- Purpose.
- Owner.
- Data sources.
- Required source capabilities.
- Metric references.
- Dimensions.
- Filters.
- Grouping.
- Aggregation.
- Currency policy.
- Accounting basis.
- Period semantics.
- Freshness requirements.
- Access policy.
- Output schema.
- Version.
- Effective dates.
- Approval status.

## 4.3 Metric Definition

A Metric Definition specifies the meaning and calculation of a measurable quantity.

It must define:

- Canonical metric identifier.
- Name.
- Business meaning.
- Formula or calculation contract.
- Numerator and denominator where relevant.
- Unit.
- Currency semantics.
- Accounting basis where applicable.
- Inclusion rules.
- Exclusion rules.
- Aggregation behavior.
- Time semantics.
- Source authorities.
- Required dimensions.
- Freshness requirements.
- Data-quality requirements.
- Version.
- Owner.
- Approval state.

A display label alone is not a canonical metric definition.

## 4.4 Reporting Dataset

A Reporting Dataset is a governed logical collection of data intended for a defined reporting purpose.

It may be materialized or virtual.

It must specify:

- Source lineage.
- Schema.
- Refresh semantics.
- Access policy.
- Data classification.
- Quality constraints.
- Version.
- Retention.
- Consumer scope.

## 4.5 Reporting Snapshot

A Reporting Snapshot identifies a reproducible reporting input state.

It may refer to:

- Source-system versions.
- Accounting-period close versions.
- Data extraction timestamps.
- Metric definition versions.
- Report definition versions.
- Transformation versions.
- Approved valuation references.

A snapshot does not need to duplicate all source data if stable references and appropriate historical reconstruction mechanisms exist.

## 4.6 Financial Statement

A Financial Statement is a governed financial representation produced under an approved accounting, contractual, or reporting framework.

It may contain:

- Reporting entity.
- Reporting period.
- Currency.
- Accounting basis.
- Statement sections.
- Opening balances.
- Activity.
- Closing balances.
- Comparative periods.
- Notes.
- Disclosures.
- Supporting schedules.
- Approval status.
- Publication status.

The statement's authority must be explicit.

A management dashboard must not be represented as a statutory financial statement merely because it displays similar information.

## 4.7 Report Execution

A Report Execution represents one attempt to generate a report.

It must track:

- Execution identifier.
- Report definition version.
- Requested scope.
- Requesting principal.
- Execution parameters.
- Source snapshot references.
- Start and completion timestamps.
- Execution status.
- Data-quality status.
- Output references.
- Errors.
- Warnings.
- Provenance.

## 4.8 Reporting Dimension

A Reporting Dimension classifies data along a governed business axis.

Examples include:

- Accounting entity.
- Merchant.
- Industry.
- Product.
- Service.
- Product category.
- Brand.
- Geography.
- Channel.
- Campaign.
- Customer segment where authorized.
- Currency.
- Accounting period.
- Commercial agreement.
- Business unit.
- Fulfillment model.
- Payment method.
- Settlement arrangement.

Dimensions must reference their canonical authorities.

## 4.9 Financial Forecast

A Financial Forecast represents a model-based estimate of future financial outcomes.

It must identify:

- Forecast definition.
- Forecast period.
- Target metric.
- Model version.
- Input data.
- Assumptions.
- Scenarios.
- Uncertainty.
- Evaluation evidence.
- Generation timestamp.
- Approval status where applicable.

A forecast is not an accounting fact.

## 4.10 Financial Scenario

A Financial Scenario describes a governed hypothetical set of assumptions and the modeled outcomes derived from them.

It must remain separate from production accounting records.

Scenario outputs must not trigger financial postings merely because a modeled result exists.

## 4.11 Report Publication

A Report Publication represents an authorized release of a report to a defined audience or destination.

It must preserve:

- Report version.
- Audience.
- Destination.
- Authorization.
- Publication timestamp.
- Data-finality status.
- Disclosure restrictions.
- Distribution history.

## 4.12 Report Lineage

Report Lineage links a report output to its source records, metric definitions, transformation rules, report definition, and execution context.

Lineage must be discoverable without embedding the entire UCOS domain model inside the reporting service.

---

# 5. REPORTING AUTHORITY MODEL

## 5.1 Authority principle

The reporting capability owns the governed presentation and analytical definitions explicitly assigned to it.

It does not automatically own the source facts that feed those definitions.

For example:

- An accounting ledger owns posted accounting entries.
- A payment system owns payment execution records.
- A settlement system owns settlement records within its authority.
- A reconciliation system owns reconciliation conclusions.
- A reporting catalog owns the canonical definition of a report or metric where that responsibility is assigned to it.

## 5.2 Source-of-truth references

Every reporting source must identify:

- Canonical source domain.
- Canonical entity type.
- Source identifier.
- Source schema or contract version.
- Source authority.
- Permitted access method.
- Refresh semantics.
- Historical availability.
- Data-quality constraints.

## 5.3 No competing financial facts

The reporting capability may maintain:

- Materialized views.
- Cached aggregates.
- Reporting snapshots.
- Analytical projections.
- Historical report outputs.
- Search indexes.
- Statistical features.

These are derived representations.

They must not become alternative canonical financial records.

## 5.4 Authoritative and derived states

The architecture must distinguish:

1. Authoritative source fact.
2. Ingested reporting record.
3. Validated reporting record.
4. Transformed reporting record.
5. Derived metric.
6. Aggregated report result.
7. Forecast or scenario result.
8. Published report.
9. Certified report output.

These states must have explicit semantics.

Cross-cutting capabilities:

- Canonical identity and authorization.
- Data governance and privacy.
- Metric and report versioning.
- Source lineage.
- Audit evidence.
- Quality monitoring.
- Retention.

- Operational observability.
- Recovery.
- Certification.

The reporting capability consumes authoritative facts and produces
derived information. It must not replace the authorities of the
source domains.

# 8. REPORT CATALOG AND LIFECYCLE

## 8.1 Report categories

The architecture must support extensible report categories, including:

- Financial statements.
- Accounting summaries.
- Merchant statements.
- Marketplace performance reports.
- Revenue reports.
- Commission reports.
- Fee reports.
- Refund reports.
- Settlement reports.
- Payout reports.
- Tax summaries.
- Reconciliation reports.
- Financial exception reports.
- Revenue variance reports.
- Cost and margin reports.
- Cash-flow reports.
- Risk-related financial reports.
- Operational finance reports.
- Management reports.
- Regulatory reports.
- Forecast reports.
- Scenario reports.

This is an illustrative taxonomy, not a hard-coded closed enumeration.

## 8.2 Report lifecycle

Proposed lifecycle:

DRAFT
  |
  v
UNDER_REVIEW
  |
  v
APPROVED
  |
  v
ACTIVE
  |
  +----> SUSPENDED
  |
  v
DEPRECATED
  |
  v
RETIRED

A report definition must retain historical versions when needed to reproduce previously generated outputs.

Retiring a report must not erase historical publication or execution evidence.

## 8.3 Report definition validation

A report definition must be rejected or held for review if it contains:

- Unknown source references.
- Unauthorized data access.
- Undefined metrics.
- Incompatible aggregation.
- Invalid currency transformations.
- Circular metric dependencies.
- Unsupported filters.
- Unbounded query behavior where prohibited.
- Missing required lineage.
- Unapproved external disclosure.
- Invalid output schema.
- Unresolved version dependencies.

## 8.4 Report templates

Templates may provide reusable presentation and calculation structures.

A template must not become a separate canonical source for metric semantics.

Every template must reference governed metric definitions and source contracts.

---

# 9. CANONICAL FINANCIAL METRIC MODEL

## 9.1 Metric catalog

The system must provide a governed catalog of financial metrics.

Every canonical metric must have:

- Unique identifier.
- Name.
- Business definition.
- Formula.
- Source references.
- Unit.
- Currency behavior.
- Time semantics.
- Aggregation behavior.
- Applicable accounting context.
- Applicable entity scope.
- Inclusion rules.
- Exclusion rules.
- Null-handling policy.
- Data-quality constraints.
- Owner.
- Version.
- Effective dates.
- Approval status.

## 9.2 Metric categories

The metric catalog should support categories such as:

- Transaction volume.
- Gross merchandise value.
- Net merchandise value.
- Revenue.
- Cost.
- Margin.
- Commission.
- Fee income.
- Merchant payable.
- Refunds.
- Tax.
- Settlement.
- Payouts.
- Receivables.
- Liabilities.
- Expenses.
- Cash movement.
- Reconciliation differences.
- Operational efficiency.
- Forecast values.
- Risk indicators.

The actual canonical taxonomy must be reconciled with existing UCOS financial definitions.

## 9.3 Metric composition

A composite metric may depend on other canonical metrics.

The system must maintain an explicit dependency graph.

Metric dependencies must be:

- Discoverable.
- Versioned.
- Validated.
- Non-circular.
- Explainable.
- Testable.

## 9.4 Metric changes

A change to a metric's meaning must not silently overwrite the historical definition.

Where the semantic meaning changes materially, the system must introduce a governed new version or identifier according to the canonical evolution policy.

## 9.5 Metric certification

A metric may be classified as:

- Draft.
- Under review.
- Approved.
- Certified.
- Deprecated.
- Retired.

The meaning of each state must be defined by governance.

A certified metric must have documented evidence of semantic correctness, source lineage, calculation validation, and access control.

---

# 10. FINANCIAL SEMANTICS AND CALCULATION GOVERNANCE

## 10.1 Explicit definitions

The system must not assume that common business terms have universally identical meanings.

Terms such as revenue, sales, gross value, net value, margin, profit, payable, settlement, and cash must have scoped definitions.

## 10.2 Gross merchandise value

A GMV definition must specify:

- Included transaction types.
- Whether cancelled orders are excluded.
- Treatment of partial cancellations.
- Treatment of refunds.
- Treatment of discounts.
- Treatment of taxes.
- Treatment of shipping.
- Treatment of failed payments.
- Treatment of pending transactions.
- Currency basis.
- Time basis.
- Source authority.

Different GMV variants must be separately defined when their semantics differ.

## 10.3 Revenue

Revenue reporting must distinguish the source commercial amount from accounting-recognized revenue.

The reporting system must consume approved accounting results for accounting revenue.

It must not infer recognized revenue from order value, payment capture, settlement, or merchant sales totals alone.

## 10.4 Margin

Margin definitions must identify their cost and revenue components.

Possible measures include:

- Gross margin.
- Contribution margin.
- Net margin.
- Merchant-level margin.
- Product-level margin.
- Campaign-level margin.

These are separate metric definitions unless an approved semantic model explicitly establishes their relationship.

## 10.5 Refund metrics

Refund metrics must distinguish:

- Refund requested.
- Refund approved.
- Refund executed.
- Refund settled.
- Refund accounted for.
- Refund reconciled.

The reporting system must not treat all refund lifecycle states as equivalent.

## 10.6 Settlement metrics

Settlement metrics must distinguish:

- Settlement calculated.
- Settlement obligation created.
- Settlement approved.
- Settlement executed.
- Settlement acknowledged.
- Settlement reconciled.

## 10.7 Financial variance

A variance report must specify:

- Comparison baseline.
- Actual measure.
- Expected measure.
- Difference formula.
- Percentage denominator.
- Currency basis.
- Period alignment.
- Missing-data behavior.
- Rounding policy.

## 10.8 Financial arithmetic

The system must use approved exact monetary representations and governed rounding.

Aggregations must not silently combine incompatible currencies or accounting bases.

Percentage metrics must define their behavior when denominators are zero, missing, negative, or otherwise invalid.

---

# 11. REPORTING PERIODS AND TEMPORAL SEMANTICS

## 11.1 Time dimensions

The reporting model must distinguish:

- Business event time.
- Source-system recording time.
- Accounting date.
- Accounting period.
- Settlement date.
- Payment execution date.
- Reporting extraction time.
- Report generation time.
- Publication time.
- Forecast target period.

These concepts must not be substituted for one another without explicit policy.

## 11.2 Period definitions

The system must support configurable reporting periods, including:

- Calendar-based periods.
- Accounting periods.
- Contractual periods.
- Operational periods.
- Rolling windows.
- Comparative windows.
- Event-relative windows.

The system must not hard-code one global reporting calendar.

## 11.3 Time zones

Where timestamps are relevant, the report definition must specify the applicable time-zone semantics.

The system must distinguish storage timestamps, event timestamps, local business dates, and accounting dates.

## 11.4 Late-arriving data

The system must identify when new source data changes a previously generated report.

It must support governed decisions to:

- Regenerate a report.
- Publish a restated version.
- Append a correction.
- Retain the previous version and disclose the difference.
- Leave the report unchanged under an approved finality policy.

The correct action depends on the report's authority and applicable policies.

## 11.5 Historical reports

Historical report reproducibility must preserve the applicable:

- Report definition version.
- Metric definition version.
- Source snapshot or version references.
- Currency conversion references.
- Transformation version.
- Reporting parameters.
- Data-quality state.
- Generation timestamp.

A report generated from a new definition must not be presented as identical to a prior report generated under a different definition.

---

# 12. FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

## 12.1 Statement types

The architecture must support extensible statement definitions, including:

- Balance sheet or equivalent financial position statement.
- Income statement or equivalent performance statement.
- Cash-flow statement.
- Trial balance.
- Account activity statement.
- Merchant financial statement.
- Settlement statement.
- Commission statement.
- Fee statement.
- Tax-related statement.
- Management accounting statement.
- Other governed financial statements.

The list does not determine which statements are legally required for a particular entity.

## 12.2 Statement authority

Every statement definition must declare whether it is:

- Operational.
- Management-oriented.
- Contractual.
- Accounting-derived.
- Statutory.
- Regulatory.
- Informational.

Its publication requirements must follow that classification.

## 12.3 Statement generation

The statement engine must:

1. Resolve the approved statement definition.
2. Validate the reporting entity.
3. Resolve the period.
4. Resolve the accounting basis.
5. Resolve the currency context.
6. Retrieve authorized source data.
7. Apply approved mapping and presentation rules.
8. Validate required totals and relationships.
9. Apply required comparative-period logic.
10. Record data-quality and completeness status.
11. Produce a versioned statement output.
12. Preserve lineage and execution evidence.
13. Route the statement through required approval.
14. Publish only when authorized.

## 12.4 Statement consistency

Statement totals must reconcile with their underlying reportable records under the applicable definitions and scope.

Any permitted difference must be explicitly governed and explained.

## 12.5 Statement finality

Statements must identify whether they are:

- Preliminary.
- Draft.
- Under review.
- Approved.
- Published.
- Restated.
- Superseded.
- Withdrawn.

A report's publication state must not be confused with the finality of its underlying accounting data.

---

# 13. MERCHANT FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

## 13.1 Purpose

Provide merchants with authorized, understandable, and traceable representations of their financial activity.

## 13.2 Statement contents

Where applicable, a merchant statement may include:

- Merchant identity reference.
- Statement identifier.
- Statement period.
- Currency.
- Opening balance.
- Sales-related entries.
- Commissions.
- Fees.
- Discounts and promotional funding.
- Tax-related entries.
- Refund-related entries.
- Chargeback-related entries.
- Adjustments.
- Reserves and holds.
- Settlement references.
- Payout references.
- Closing balance.
- Outstanding exceptions.
- Statement status.
- Generation timestamp.
- Version.

The actual contents must follow the merchant agreement and approved financial reporting model.

## 13.3 Merchant isolation

A merchant must only access information authorized for that merchant and its permitted organizational scope.

The system must enforce isolation at the service, query, export, cache, and publication layers as applicable.

A client-supplied merchant identifier must never be sufficient proof of access.

## 13.4 Merchant-facing balance semantics

Every displayed balance must have an explicit meaning.

Examples include:

- Posted accounting balance.
- Amount pending settlement.
- Amount eligible for settlement.
- Amount held in reserve.
- Amount subject to dispute.
- Amount paid out.
- Amount awaiting reconciliation.

The system must not label these distinct amounts simply as an undifferentiated "available balance."

## 13.5 Statement corrections

When a statement changes, the system must preserve its previous version and provide the applicable correction or restatement relationship.

The publication model must prevent a merchant from mistaking a corrected statement for an unchanged historical version.

---

# 14. REPORTING DATA ARCHITECTURE

## 14.1 Data acquisition

The system must retrieve information through authorized, governed source interfaces.

Source integration must not rely on undocumented direct access to another domain's internal database.

## 14.2 Data quality

Every material dataset must define appropriate quality constraints.

Possible checks include:

- Completeness.
- Validity.
- Uniqueness.
- Referential integrity.
- Currency consistency.
- Temporal consistency.
- Accounting-period consistency.
- Source freshness.
- Duplicate detection.
- Reconciliation-state consistency.
- Schema compatibility.

## 14.3 Missing data

Missing data must be represented explicitly.

The system must distinguish:

- Zero.
- Null.
- Unknown.
- Not applicable.
- Not yet received.
- Not authorized for disclosure.
- Failed retrieval.
- Incomplete processing.
- Not reconciled.

These states must not be silently converted into zero.

## 14.4 Materialized datasets

Materialized reporting datasets may be used to improve query performance.

They must have:

- An owner.
- Source lineage.
- Schema version.
- Refresh policy.
- Freshness indicator.
- Rebuild procedure.
- Access policy.
- Retention policy.
- Quality checks.

## 14.5 Data retention

Retention must follow approved governance, accounting, regulatory, privacy, and contractual policies.

The reporting system must not retain every source record indefinitely merely to simplify report generation.

## 14.6 Data minimization

Reports should retrieve only the information necessary for the approved purpose.

Personal or sensitive information must not be copied into broad analytical datasets without a documented, authorized need.

---

# 15. ANALYTICS AND FINANCIAL DECISION INTELLIGENCE

## 15.1 Analytical capabilities

The architecture may support:

- Trend analysis.
- Variance analysis.
- Comparative performance.
- Revenue decomposition.
- Cost analysis.
- Margin analysis.
- Merchant performance analysis.
- Product and category performance.
- Channel analysis.
- Campaign performance.
- Settlement and payout trends.
- Refund trends.
- Exception analysis.
- Forecasting.
- Scenario modeling.
- Sensitivity analysis.
- Risk indicators.
- Anomaly detection.

These are reporting and analytical capabilities, not independent sources of financial authority.

## 15.2 Drill-down

A user must be able to drill down from an aggregate metric to authorized supporting records where permitted.

The system must preserve:

- Metric definition.
- Aggregation logic.
- Filter context.
- Source references.
- Access restrictions.
- Data-finality status.

## 15.3 Comparative analysis

Comparisons must specify whether periods are aligned by:

- Calendar duration.
- Accounting period.
- Business days.
- Transaction lifecycle state.
- Commercial campaign.
- Other approved comparison logic.

Comparisons must disclose non-comparable conditions where material.

## 15.4 Scenario analysis

A scenario must have explicit assumptions and a unique identity.

Scenario changes must not modify production accounting records.

Scenario results must identify assumptions and distinguish them from observed facts.

## 15.5 Forecasting

Forecasts must identify:

- Target metric.
- Forecast horizon.
- Model version.
- Input data.
- Assumptions.
- Uncertainty or confidence information where appropriate.
- Known limitations.
- Generation time.
- Evaluation evidence.

Forecasts must not be presented as guaranteed outcomes.

## 15.6 Financial recommendations

A recommendation generated from analytics must identify the underlying metrics, assumptions, and constraints.

The reporting capability may recommend investigation or further analysis.

It must not autonomously execute payments, settlement, accounting adjustments, or other financial actions unless a separate, explicitly authorized workflow governs that action.

---

# 16. REPORT EXECUTION AND DISTRIBUTION

## 16.1 Execution modes

The architecture may support:

- Interactive reports.
- Scheduled reports.
- Event-triggered reports.
- On-demand exports.
- Batch reports.
- Period-close reports.
- Merchant statements.
- Approved regulatory reports.
- Analytical snapshots.

## 16.2 Execution lifecycle

Proposed lifecycle:

REQUESTED
   |
   v
AUTHORIZATION_CHECK
   |
   v
DEFINITION_VALIDATION
   |
   v
SOURCE_RESOLUTION
   |
   v
DATA_QUALITY_VALIDATION
   |
   v
COMPUTATION
   |
   v
OUTPUT_VALIDATION
   |
   v
COMPLETED
   |
   v
APPROVAL_IF_REQUIRED
   |
   v
PUBLICATION_IF_AUTHORIZED

Exceptional states:

- REJECTED.
- FAILED.
- CANCELLED.
- PARTIALLY_COMPLETED.
- WAITING_FOR_SOURCE.
- WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL.
- QUARANTINED.

## 16.3 Scheduling

Scheduling must support governed recurrence and event-driven execution without hard-coding a single calendar or time zone.

Schedules must be versioned and auditable.

## 16.4 Subscriptions

Subscriptions must define:

- Subscriber.
- Report.
- Scope.
- Schedule.
- Delivery destination.
- Authorization.
- Expiration.
- Failure handling.
- Revocation behavior.

A subscription must not preserve access after the subscriber loses the required authorization.

## 16.5 Publication

Publication must verify the recipient's authorization at the time required by the applicable policy.

Sensitive financial reports must not be distributed to unverified recipients.

## 16.6 Export

Export formats must be extensible through governed contracts.

Possible formats include structured data, spreadsheets, printable documents, and machine-readable interfaces.

The exact format list must not become a limitation on future interoperability.

## 16.7 Export safety

Exports must enforce:

- Authorization.
- Scope restrictions.
- Data minimization.
- Auditability.
- Appropriate encryption.
- Expiration where applicable.
- Secure delivery.
- Controlled re-download.
- Revocation or invalidation where supported.

---

# 17. API CONTRACT MODEL

## 17.1 API principles

All reporting APIs must:

- Use canonical identifiers.
- Enforce authorization.
- Validate inputs.
- Resolve metric and report versions.
- Preserve execution lineage.
- Define pagination.
- Define query limits.
- Support correlation identifiers.
- Avoid ambiguous financial semantics.
- Return explicit data-freshness states.
- Protect sensitive information.
- Support versioned contracts.
- Provide controlled error responses.

The following are proposed logical operations, not claims of existing endpoints.

## 17.2 Report registry APIs

- `GET /reporting/reports`
- `POST /reporting/reports`
- `GET /reporting/reports/{reportId}`
- `GET /reporting/reports/{reportId}/versions`
- `POST /reporting/reports/{reportId}/validate`
- `POST /reporting/reports/{reportId}/submit-for-approval`
- `POST /reporting/reports/{reportId}/approve`
- `POST /reporting/reports/{reportId}/deprecate`

## 17.3 Metric APIs

- `GET /reporting/metrics`
- `GET /reporting/metrics/{metricId}`
- `GET /reporting/metrics/{metricId}/versions`
- `POST /reporting/metrics/{metricId}/validate`
- `GET /reporting/metrics/{metricId}/lineage`
- `GET /reporting/metrics/{metricId}/quality`

## 17.4 Report execution APIs

- `POST /reporting/executions`
- `GET /reporting/executions/{executionId}`
- `POST /reporting/executions/{executionId}/cancel`
- `GET /reporting/executions/{executionId}/lineage`
- `GET /reporting/executions/{executionId}/quality`
- `GET /reporting/executions/{executionId}/output`

## 17.5 Financial statement APIs

- `POST /reporting/statements/generate`
- `GET /reporting/statements/{statementId}`
- `GET /reporting/statements/{statementId}/versions`
- `GET /reporting/statements/{statementId}/lineage`
- `POST /reporting/statements/{statementId}/submit-for-approval`
- `POST /reporting/statements/{statementId}/publish`

## 17.6 Merchant statement APIs

- `GET /reporting/merchant-statements`
- `POST /reporting/merchant-statements/generate`
- `GET /reporting/merchant-statements/{statementId}`
- `GET /reporting/merchant-statements/{statementId}/versions`
- `GET /reporting/merchant-statements/{statementId}/lineage`

Merchant scoping and authorization must be enforced by the service, not trusted to caller-supplied filters.

## 17.7 Analytics APIs

- `POST /reporting/analytics/queries`
- `GET /reporting/analytics/queries/{queryId}`
- `POST /reporting/analytics/scenarios`
- `GET /reporting/analytics/scenarios/{scenarioId}`
- `POST /reporting/analytics/forecasts`
- `GET /reporting/analytics/forecasts/{forecastId}`

## 17.8 Distribution APIs

- `POST /reporting/publications`
- `GET /reporting/publications/{publicationId}`
- `POST /reporting/subscriptions`
- `GET /reporting/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`
- `POST /reporting/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/revoke`
- `GET /reporting/publications/{publicationId}/delivery-status`

## 17.9 Quality and governance APIs

- `GET /reporting/quality/issues`
- `GET /reporting/quality/datasets/{datasetId}`
- `GET /reporting/definitions/{definitionId}/dependencies`
- `GET /reporting/definitions/{definitionId}/audit`
- `GET /reporting/certification/{artifactId}`

## 17.10 API result semantics

The API must distinguish:

- Request accepted.
- Request rejected.
- Execution pending.
- Execution completed.
- Execution completed with warnings.
- Execution failed.
- Output generated.
- Output approved.
- Output published.
- Delivery completed.
- Delivery failed.
- Data incomplete.
- Data stale.
- Data provisional.
- Data final under the applicable policy.

A generated report is not necessarily approved for publication.
